findings.title: Mutual exclusion check between `age` and `timestamp` ignores `0`
findings.body: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, `validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`. Because `0` is falsy in Python, a report containing `"age": 0` alongside a valid `timestamp` (or `"timestamp": 0` alongside a valid `age`, where `0` is explicitly allowed by `min_value=0`) will bypass both validation checks instead of raising a `ValidationError`. These checks should test `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp") is not None`.

findings.title: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` by position instead of by node_id
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=id) for id in error_ids]`, calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, and then iterates `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.get_multi` returns a dict mapping `node_id -> data` whose keys are neither guaranteed to be in `node_ids` order nor guaranteed to include missing keys in all backends. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can associate an `event_id` with the wrong event payload or silently drop/shift entries when some events are missing from nodestore. Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

findings.title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
findings.body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` directly when `!searchQuery.trim()` (lines 61-63), and only applies `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` inside the `filter` call when `searchQuery` is non-empty (lines 65-69). As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are visible in the default (unsearched) view and only disappear once the user types into the search box. The `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter should be applied before checking `searchQuery.trim()`.
